title: The ten sefiros of kelipa: the opposite that comes first
overview: The last chapter of the book turns to *zeh l'umas zeh*, the ten *sefiros* of *kelipa*. *Kelipa* is the peel that grows before the fruit and the placenta that comes before the child: waste, from the breaking of the vessels, and yet it protects the fruit and feeds the baby. Whatever spreads from the essence has an opposing power from the same essence, a *menaged* that opposes the will in every detail, and the hiding comes first: first darkness, then light. The breaking was in the *middos* of *bina*: the analysis is right and the "therefore" goes wrong, and the *chachma* of *kelipa* is no wisdom, only cunning. Rabbi Markel applies this as he goes: to making the Torah agree with science, which he calls a heresy dressed as reason, to abortion, to sources twisted to argue against the Rebbe. Then the *partzuf* of *kelipa*, *Adam Belial*, a mirror image whose depth is the will for evil; *kelipas noga*, from the self-feeling of *Atzilus*, a good man who knows he is good, down to *Asiya*, which loves judgement; and the three impure *kelipos*, which wait for the future, "meaning tomorrow". The book ends with the *hadran*.

sections.title: Kelipa is the peel that comes before the fruit, and grows it
sections.summary: The chapter opens a whole new ten *sefiros*, those of *kelipa*: the waste from the breaking of the vessels, which comes first like a peel or a placenta, and like them protects and feeds what comes after.

phrases.he: (נד) ולהבין דרך פרט בהשתלשלות דאת זה לעומת זה כו'
בעשר ספירות דקליפה דאבי"ע
phrases.en: now we're talking about a whole new ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: כו', הנה יש להקדים בשרש בחינת הקליפה מהו דהנה ידוע בטעם שם קליפה, כמו קליפת הפרי שהוא הפסולת שבכל דבר, שבא מצד תערובת טוב ורע כו' מסיבת שבירת הכלים כו' ז' מלכים שמתו ונפלו למטה כו'

blocks.text: Now the *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) of *zeh l'umas zeh* (this opposite that) in detail: a whole new ten *sefiros*, the ten *sefiros* of *kelipa* (lit. husk; what conceals G-dliness) in *ABYA*. First, what is *kelipa* at its root? It is named for the peel of a fruit, the *pesoles* (waste) of a thing, which comes from the mixture of good and evil: the breaking of the vessels, the seven kings who died and fell.

phrases.he: וקליפה קדמה לפרי, כמו בצמיחת כל פרי שהקליפה תצמח תחלה,
וכמו השליא
phrases.en: like the placenta

phrases.he: לולד שהוא בא מן הפסולת שבטיפה כו'

blocks.text: The *kelipa* comes before the fruit, as every fruit grows its peel first, and as the *shilya* (placenta) comes before the child. And this tells something about those people: they are basically our *kelipa*.

From what the text says, the *kelipa* has a good purpose. The peel protects the fruit, and the *shilya* actually grows the baby: it gives the baby its nourishment. What goes from the mother to the *shilya* is the impure blood, the *dam nidda*, what would otherwise have been one of the most impure things, and the *shilya* makes it the baby's food.

So it is with us. As the Rebbe told Rabbi Markel in letters, spoken of a few days before, these people are not stealing from us: they are going to bring us our nourishment. They are going to grow us, as the *shilya* grows the baby and the *kelipa* grows the fruit.

sections.title: The menaged: whatever comes from the essence has its opposite, in every detail
sections.summary: Everything that spreads from the essence has an opposing power from the same essence: pain against delight, a reason against the will, a servant who opposes his master in every detail. And that opposition comes with a reason of its own.

phrases.he: ושרש הדברים ידוע, דגם בבחינת התענוג יש בחינת המנגד אליו, שהוא הצער היפך הענג, והוא נגע היפך אותיות ענג )ופשע היפך אותיות שפע כו') כי כל דבר מה שבא בבחינת התפשטות מן העצם, ודאי יש כח המנגד אליו שבא גם כן מן העצם על כן גם בבחינת התפשטות אור התענוג והרצון יש כח היפוכו המנגדו, שהוא על דרך משל כאשר ימנעו לאותו תענוג או שיהיה דבר המנגד, היפך העונג, הוא שנקרא צער ויסורין כו'

blocks.text: The root of it: even in *taanug* (delight) there is a *menaged* (an opposite), pain, the reverse of delight; *nega* (affliction) is the letters of *oneg* (delight) reversed, and *pesha* (sin) of *shefa* (flow). Whatever spreads from the essence has an opposing power that also comes from the essence. When the delight is withheld, or its opposite comes, that is pain and suffering: the same power, as learned before.

phrases.he: וכן ממילא בחכמה וטעם לתענוג ורצון יש המנגד, להיות טעם למנגד לרצון וכן המדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה כו'
וכמו עבד העובר ומנגד לרצון האדון,
הרי בכל פרטי הדברים שברצון זה מנגד כו'
phrases.en: In every single *prat* is *menaged*

blocks.text: So too in *chachma*, the reason for the delight and the will: there is a reason for the *menaged*, against the will, and so in the *middos*, thought, speech and action. Like a servant who goes against his master's will. **In every single *prat* is *menaged***: he opposes every detail of the will.

A letter of the Rebbe says: just look at what your enemies want. If they want it, there is something wrong with it. That is this line: one who is *menaged* is *menaged* in all the *pratim* (details), so whatever he wants, you know it has a problem.

If the Israelis would realize that about Arafat: whatever he wants, even to make peace, even to give you a present, there is something wrong with it, as the Trojans found out. With the *l'umas zeh*, it does not matter what it is or how nice it looks.

sensitivity.reason: Applies the line to Arafat and to Israel's peace-making: whatever he offers, even peace, is wrong.
sensitivity.publishable: Whatever the *menaged* wants, even to give you a present, there is something wrong with it, as the Trojans found out. With the *l'umas zeh*, it does not matter what it is or how nice it looks.

blocks.text: And the *menaged* comes with a *sevara* (a line of reasoning), a *sechel*, as the text just said. Its reasoning goes: let us tell these people that the Torah really agrees with science, so it will not sound so stupid to them, and they will start keeping Shabbos and mitzvos; that way we will slowly get them. Look at what it says and you see its whole plan: to sneak in with a little white lie, so you will agree to a little thing that, after all, is not evil. And really, it is going to slowly get you.

blocks.title: Heresy is worse than idol worship
blocks.text: And really it is a heresy, worse than *avoda zara* (idol worship): from *avoda zara* one does *teshuva* more easily. Look at what the *Rambam* says of a heretic. Menashe did all the *avoda zara* and then did *teshuva*. Achav and the like did not, yet the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) still sent them prophets to urge them: the gates were open, they only had to do it. But of *Acher* a voice said that everyone can do *teshuva* except *Acher*. Nothing stands in the way of *teshuva*, and he could have; but the gates were closed.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the teaching that the Torah agrees with science, as some outreach presents it, a heresy, and heresy worse than idol worship.

blocks.text: This is the worst kind of thing: not a *midda* like anger, of the *middos*, thought, speech and action the text speaks of, but a cold *sevara*, *Chabad* (chachma, bina and daas) of *kelipa*. As the *Tanya* says, though it looks like nothing, it makes the whole brain impure, and with something you do not even realize is evil. It is a *kefira* (denial) of how the *Aibershter* created the world: of *hashgacha pratis* (providence over each detail), of the specific creation of Adam, of *sefer, sippur v'sofer*. The world is not a movie set that started in the middle. A total *kefira*, dressed in many garments: as the *Aibershter* is dressed in many garments, so can the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination) be.

And it is *davka* intellectual. It says: how could science be wrong? And I am not telling you the Torah is wrong and science is right; I am only showing you how the Torah really says like science. Then they come up with lies: the *Ramban* said such a thing, or Rabbi Yitzchak of Acco, or Rashi; on the Aish site they even quoted Yonasan ben Uziel and misquoted Rashi. But Rashi says seven days, and seven days is seven days. Rashi never said such a thing.

sensitivity.reason: Names an outreach organization's website and says it misquotes sources.

phrases.he: וכך את זה לעומת זה עשה כו' שיהיה בחינת מנגד, והוא הנקרא פסולת וקליפה והסתר שקדם תחלה כו'

blocks.text: So the *menaged* comes with *chachma* and a reason. And so *zeh l'umas zeh* was made: the *menaged*, called *pesoles* and *kelipa*, the hiding that comes first. But from our side it is a good thing. For them it is *kefira*; for us it is *mamash* (actually) the plan. The *yetzer hara* told them his plan, to use this to pull in people: for them he is the *yetzer hara*, for us he is *mamash* bringing us the people.

The Kabbalah Centre and their kabbalists will bring in people, and the people will look and say, wait a minute, something is wrong here. And the *yetzer hara* will come to us, because the *Chassidus* we teach is made to addict the *yetzer hara*, through the *nefesh habehamis* (the animal soul): the worst addiction there is. The *Aibershter* created the *yetzer hara* and a *tavlin* (spice) for it: the *yetzer hara* has the drug to addict everybody else, and we have the drug to addict him. So look who is coming to us: the witches, the warlocks, the vampires, all the crazy people. Sooner or later they end up by us, because by us it is like a *shilya*, a *kelipa*.

sections.title: First darkness, then light
sections.summary: The hiding comes before every light: that is the order, first darkness and then light, as the nations were great before Israel. For us the darkness is only a sign that our light is coming.

phrases.he: והוא על ידי בחינת הצמצום והסתר שקודם כל אור ושפע רצון ותענוג וחכמה כו' כמו מי יודע עוז אפיך וכיראתך עברתך כו' שהוא בחינת המנגד לרצון, שם יתכן הכעס וחרון אף על בחינת המנגד ועובר הרצון כו', עד שחמת יהו״ה על ראש רשעים יחול כו' (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ברישא חשוכא,
על כן עזי אומות העולם מסגי ברישא כו')
phrases.en: The strong people of the nations were big first, before the Jews were big

blocks.text: The *kelipa* and hiding come first, through the *tzimtzum* (contraction) and hiding that precede every light, *ratzon* (will), *taanug* and *chachma*. That is the proper order, the order of the *Aibershter*'s people: *b'reisha chashocha* (first darkness), and then *nehora* (light). He reads on, of anger against the *menaged*, without comment.

As it says elsewhere of *b'reisha chashocha*: **The strong people of the nations were big first, before the Jews were big**. So too there were first the kings of Esav, and then the kings of Israel. By us it is *davka* the opposite: the darkness is only *bilbul* (confusion). There is a big *tzimtzum* up there, and this darkness is because our light is going to come.

sections.title: The breaking is in the "therefore", and the wisdom of kelipa is a con
sections.summary: The breaking was in the lower *sefiros* of *bina*, the *middos* drawn from the analysis: the analysis is correct and the conclusion goes wrong, because it is thought out from the outside. In *chachma* only the outside fell, and its *chachma* is no wisdom but cunning.

phrases.he: והנה ידוע דעיקר השבירה בתערובות טוב ורע ממש היה רק בבחינת ס"ג שהוא בבחינת ז׳ תחתונים דבינה שהן בחינת המדות שבשכל שמולידים המדות שבלב, מדות רעים כמו כעס ורציחה ותאוה רעה ואהבה ויראה רעים וניצוח והתפארות לרע כו'

blocks.text: The main breaking, a real mixture of good and evil, was only in *SaG*, the seven lower *sefiros* of *bina*: the *middos* in the intellect that give birth to the *middos* of the heart, bad *middos* like anger, murder, bad desire, bad love and fear. In *chachma* there was no breaking; only its outside fell, and that is the root of the external wisdoms.

As discussed earlier: the original *bina sheb'bina* (bina within bina) is the analysis, and the *middos* are what is called the *uvchein*, the "therefore". Look at any *kelipa* and you see that the analysis is correct.

For instance, everybody is making a big to-do about homosexuals, and there is a much worse thing: abortion. In numbers it is a holocaust going on, a secret one that people ignore, maybe even bigger. The Holocaust was six million, some eighteen million all told, maybe forty million with what Stalin did; the abortions of the last forty years worldwide, he thinks, are in the hundreds of millions. And yet, where is the *shevira* (the breaking)?

sensitivity.reason: Abortion as a holocaust bigger than the Holocaust, set against the attention paid to homosexuals.

blocks.text: The *shevira* is not in the analysis. Part of the analysis is that there are a lot of people in the world. That is true. But the *uvchein*, by him, is "so shall they increase": that is what the *Aibershter* wants, not only for Jews to increase but the settling of the world, "be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth." The *Aibershter* likes the world and likes people, as was said the day before: though it is nothing, now that He has it He likes it. He likes children. Or: a lot of people are going hungry. True. So the *uvchein* is to figure out how to feed them, a distribution problem: plant the Sahara; look what they did with Israel. Other *uvchein*s can come out. The analysis is correct.

There are all kinds of analyses: a lot of children do not get a proper education, or will grow up in bad situations, with starvation. The conclusion: good, so let's kill them. A good *uvchein*: we will solve all the world's problems. And the butterflies will not have to worry about the ecology; with all these people at the beach soon there will be no sunlight left, and what will the trees do? Kill everybody, and there will be more room for the butterflies and the bunny rabbits, no one destroying their habitat, the sun will live ten billion years longer, and no global warming.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks ecology, global warming and the balance of nature as reasons to kill people.
sensitivity.publishable: There are all kinds of analyses: a lot of children do not get a proper education, or will grow up in bad situations, with starvation. The conclusion: good, so let's kill them. A good *uvchein*: we will solve all the world's problems.

blocks.text: So the *shevira* is not in the actual analysis, the fact, but in the *uvchein*, the solution you came up with. And the text first says it was only in *SaG*, but then that the outside of *Abba* fell too: so it touches even the inside. If there were no problem with the *hanacha* (premise) somehow, the act would not come out wrong. The problem is not in the real premise; it is in the *chitzoniyus* (outside) of the premise.

blocks.question: If the premise is right and the hisbonenus is right, how could the act come out wrong?
blocks.text: Exactly because it was the outside. As in chapters 24 to 26: the *mazalos*, then how it comes down, then the act of *Zeir Anpin*; if one is not the inside, the next level will not be the inside either. They are thinking externally, not internally. Not only do they not connect it to the *Aibershter*; they do not even think properly by the tree of knowledge of good. That is not from the *Aibershter*, but it is solid *bina sheb'bina*: if you would really sit and think properly, you could come up with a better act.

These people are not really sitting and thinking with a real *hisbonenus* (contemplation). They come up with a fast act and run with it, and most of them do not even know who came up with it. You know who came up with it? Our good buddy the *yetzer hara*. They run with this *sechel* as if it were a real *sechel*, and it is not a *sechel* at all: as the text will explain, it is not *chachma* but cunning. From it come the *middos* of the heart, anger and murder, bad desire, love and fear.

blocks.text: In *chachma* there was no breaking; only its *chitzoniyus* fell, because it was outside, and that is the root of the external wisdoms. It is also "I, wisdom, dwell with cunning," and *Arami oved avi*. The *Arami* is a *ramai*, a con artist, as Lavan was. *Avi*, my father, is *Abba*, the *chachma* of holiness, and the *Arami* is the *chachma* of *kelipa*, which makes a person lose his proper father: it makes a *bilbul* in people's heads, and really it is cheating.

Not a single *gadol* said that. What they say is all based on some scientist, Schroeder, and then they make it fit what the *Rambam* said. But the *Rambam* did not say that: ask him and he would say it was seven days; ask Rashi, seven days, *kipshuto* (literally). Ask them whether Adam came from a monkey, and they would say no, it was a specific creation. That is *pshat* in the Torah.

blocks.title: Rosenberg's Zohar: devolution, not evolution
blocks.text: On Darwinism, as in an email he sent: Yudel Rosenberg (he gropes for the name), who translated the *Zohar* into Hebrew, writes that according to the *Zohar* there was not evolution but devolution: the apes came from people. There were apparently two points, a devolution by Kayin and, he thinks, another by the people of the Tower of Bavel; by Kayin he knows for sure. Rosenberg writes that maybe this is where "Darwin the *meshuga*" got his ideas. He is of the school of the real kabbalists, a real *ben Torah*, with *haskamos* (approbations) from practically every *gadol* in Europe, Rabbi Chaim Berlin among them, and of course the Rebbe Rashab. For Lubavitch there is no need to go to Rosenberg: we have the letters of the Rebbe, straight, that this is a heresy. So where do they get that the *gedolim* said such a thing?

blocks.title: Rabbi Yitzchak of Acco
blocks.text: Or they dig up Rabbi Yitzchak of Acco: who ever heard of him? A listener objects that he was a real kabbalist, and Rabbi Markel agrees: a real, true, big kabbalist. But there is the prohibition of Rabbi Chaim Vital, in the name of the *Arizal*, against studying anyone after the *Ramban*, and Rabbi Yitzchak of Acco was a student of the *Ramban*. There are two reasons: some of them did not know what they were talking about, and the others, you will not know what they are talking about. Nor, he thinks, is he speculation: his writing is very mystical and hard to understand, but if you know *Kabbala* you see from his calculations right away what he means. There is nothing wrong with it; the problem is how they translated it.
So these people make up stories, and it is a con: they stick something in as if it were the opinion of the Torah, bring various quotes, and you can see the con *mamash*.

blocks.title: The rabbi who wrote against kefiya
blocks.text: A rabbi, one of the YU type, wrote a whole thing against what the Rebbe says about *kefiya* (compelling) of the *goyim*, bringing various opinions. One says that in our days you cannot kill a *goy*; but the *Rambam* never said you could: for that you need a *beis din* that can kill, and that is not what *kefiya* means. Another, the *Rema* or someone, says that even when the Sanhedrin had the power, you could not kill him before the sentence was passed; you had to take him to *beis din*. So how does that disprove what the Rebbe said? He totally does not understand what he is talking about.

blocks.text: Both the *Rambam* and the Rebbe in his book say this is something Moshe told us *mipi hagevura* (from the mouth of the Almighty): that one is to compel the *goyim*. When they say that, it means a *halacha l'Moshe miSinai* (a law given to Moshe at Sinai), and the *Rambam* does not say it of everything. Some things he calls not even Torah law but rabbinic: *Eruvin*, being learned now, is not a mitzva of the Torah at all. From the Torah you may carry in a whole walled city, and from a house to the yard to another house when all are fenced in, with no *eruv*; the *eruv* is from the *beis din* of Shlomo HaMelech. Other things are disputes, and the *Rambam* rules one way. But hardly ever do they say a thing was told to Moshe *mipi hagevura*; when they do, there is no argument at all.

Like lighting a fire on Shabbos, which the *Rambam* calls *halacha l'Moshe miSinai*, and nobody disagrees with him. All the other opinions that rabbi brought, he twisted, and he thinks he is right: he is a rabbi, he is helping out, saving us from the Lubavitcher Rebbe. They do not think it is a *kefira*. That is what it says: first the *yetzer hara* comes and tells you to do a mitzva, and they think it is a mitzva. That is *Arami oved avi*: the *Arami* messed up their brains, and they cannot think straight anymore. It is cunning, the *chachma* of *kelipa*.

blocks.text: **It's a *chachma* to do bad**: so their whole thing is bad, even what does not look like heresy, all their nice-looking sermons. They are wise to do evil and not to do good, on anything. **Really they're not *chachamim***: it is only *armumis* (cunning) and falsehood. *Chachma* means *chachmas ha'emes* (the wisdom of truth), this teaching. If they do not hold of it, their whole *Yiddishkeit* is cunning and falsehood, and what they want is your money. "As is known": who doesn't know this?

sections.title: The pleasures of this world, and the evil of the middos that only kills
sections.summary: From the higher delight only the outside came down, the root of the pleasures of this world; but the main evil is in the *middos*, which come down to accusers whose whole life is to kill and, in this world, to murderers. In the future they will be refined away.

phrases.he: וגם מבחינת התענוג העליון ירד בחינת החיצוניות,
וזהו שרש להתהוות תענוגי עולם הזה
phrases.en: The whole *chitzoniyus* is the *hishavus* of where the *taanugei olam hazeh* come from

blocks.text: From the higher *taanug* too the outside came down, the root of the pleasures of this world. **The whole *chitzoniyus* is the *hishavus* of where the *taanugei olam hazeh* come from**: even *Keser* was affected, to a degree, as a listener puts it. The pleasures of this world: Las Vegas, Hollywood, Disneyland.

phrases.he: אבל עיקר הרע הוא במדות
phrases.en: But the main *ra* is *davka* the *middos*

phrases.he: עד שנסתעפו למטה מטה בקליפה דעשיה המקטרגים הרעים לפעול רע בפועל ממש,
שכל חיותם אינו רק להמית
phrases.en: The whole *chayus* is only to kill

phrases.he: כמו שלוחי המות כו' ולמטה בזה העולם הן המזיקים כנחשים וחיות שטורפים כו' והרוצחים במין האדם

blocks.text: **But the main *ra* is *davka* the *middos***, which come down lower and lower into the *kelipa* of *Asiya*: the accusers who do actual evil. **The whole *chayus* is only to kill**, like agents of death. Up to now you could see it *mamash* in Germany, may their name be blotted out: angels of death *mamash*. But really *Amalek* is the *Keser* and *chachma* of *kelipa*, the *shaar hanun* (the fiftieth gate) of *kelipa*: Haman.

Below, in this world, they are the harmful things, snakes and beasts of prey, and the murderers among men: the total evil. And it is not only those who kill bodies; there is a different type of murder, the murder the Greeks wanted. The Rebbe says that is why *Shaarei Orah* is for Chanukah: to kill a person's soul is worse than to kill his body.

phrases.he: ולכך לעתיד לבא שיבוער הרע, כתיב לא ירעו ולא ישחיתו כו', לפי שאז יובררו שיורי ז' מלכים שלא נתבררו עדיין כידוע

blocks.text: So in the future, when the evil is burned away, it is written, "they will not harm and will not destroy": even the animals, there will not be any bad animals. For then the remnants of the seven kings not yet refined will be refined, a *birur* (refinement) all the way down to the physical.

The *bilbul* that starts up there is what goes farther and farther down, until, when it hits the street, you get a murderer. Ask where murderers come from, and everybody will tell you he was not educated properly, and that is why he became *frei* (irreligious). By then it is already Hell's Angels; and it does start with the education.

sections.title: Adam Belial: the partzuf of kelipa, a mirror turned over
sections.summary: *Kelipa* has a whole *partzuf* of its own, *Adam Belial*, whose head, *Keser* and *Atik*, is the depth of evil: the will for every bad thing. It mirrors holiness exactly, only reversed, and so the worst of it is not the murderer in the street but the philosophers.

phrases.he: ויש בחינת ציור אדם באת זה לעומת זה דקליפה כו' ונקרא אדם בליעל, והוא בחינת זעיר אנפין דקליפה כמו ויאבק איש עמו כו' בחינת המדות עם המוחין דאבא ואמא דקליפה, עד בחינת כתר ועתיק יומין דקליפה שנקרא עומק רע,
שהוא עומק הרצון והתענוג לכל דבר רע,
phrases.en: The *ratzon* for all the bad things

phrases.he: שהוא מקור לכל רצון רע ונקרא בזוהר כתרין דמסאבותא ובלשון הגמרא שערי טומאה כו'

blocks.text: There is also the form of a man in the *kelipa* opposite holiness, called *Adam Belial*, the *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) of *kelipa*, like "a man wrestled with him": a whole *partzuf* (stature).

But it is an upside-down *partzuf*: it goes down, not up. The whole thing is upside down; their brain is in their behind. *Belial* means they are not going to go up but down: the ten *sefiros* of *kelipa* are upside down, a downward motion. And the man who wrestled is the one fighting with Yaakov.

sensitivity.publishable: But it is an upside-down *partzuf*: it goes down, not up. The whole thing is upside down. *Belial* means they are not going to go up but down: the ten *sefiros* of *kelipa* are upside down, a downward motion. And the man who wrestled is the one fighting with Yaakov.

blocks.text: Its *Keser* and *Atik Yomin* are called *omek ra* (the depth of evil): the depth of the will and the delight for every evil thing. **The *ratzon* for all the bad things**: the source of every bad will. *Keser* and *Atik* are the *omek* (depth), the deepest part.

blocks.question: If Keser and Atik are the deepest part, does that mean they are the lowest?
blocks.text: Not really: it is straight, because *omek tov* (the depth of good) is the same. It is *zeh l'umas zeh*, like a mirror: whatever is here is exactly the same over there. By the good the head is in the *omek*, the will for everything good, and so by the evil. It works the same way, only reversed: it goes from *Keser* to *Malchus*, and its *Malchus* is higher up than its *Keser*.

It is the reverse; so who are the worst people of all? Not the murderer in the street: the philosophers. They are the *omek*, the *chachma*; they have *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina*, the philosophy behind this whole thing. It still starts in the *mochin* (the intellect) and goes down to the *middos*, only upside down, and it is called sorcery and the deeds of sorcery; in the language of the Gemara, the gates of impurity.

sensitivity.reason: Calls philosophers the worst people of all, worse than murderers, and the head of the kelipa.
sensitivity.publishable: It is the reverse; so where is the worst of it? Not in the murderer in the street but in the *omek*, the *chachma*: *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina*, the philosophy behind this whole thing. It still starts in the *mochin* (the intellect) and goes down to the *middos*, only upside down, and it is called sorcery and the deeds of sorcery; in the language of the Gemara, the gates of impurity.

sections.title: Kelipas noga through the worlds: from feeling oneself to loving judgement
sections.summary: *Noga* of *Atzilus* has no evil, only a good man who feels how good he is; as it comes down it becomes *chesed* for his own honor, anger for his own honor, an accuser in *Yetzira*, and in *Asiya* a leech that lives to judge.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל יש בחינת עשר ספירות דקליפת נוגה באבי"ע אך בחינת נוגה דאצילות אין בו רע כלל, וכמו שכתוב לא יגורך רע כו',
רק שהוא בחינת היש המורגש ובולט ביותר,
phrases.en: that he feels how great and good he is

phrases.he: כמו בחינת החסד המורגש באדם להתפאר בו שהוא עושה דבר חסד
או בחכמה מרגיש חכמתו ביותר,
phrases.en: he's a real *chacham*, but he knows what a *chacham* he is

phrases.he: וכך כל מדותיו ומעלותיו יודע ומרגיש בבחינת בליטה גדולה

blocks.text: In general there are ten *sefiros* of *kelipas noga* (the translucent husk) in *ABYA*. But *noga* of *Atzilus* has no evil at all, as it says, "evil shall not dwell with You"; it is only the *yesh* (existence) felt and standing out most: **that he feels how great and good he is**. Like the *chesed* a person feels and takes pride in: someone who is really a big *gvir* (rich man) and very proud of it. It is a hundred percent good. He is a good guy, and he knows he is a good guy.

Or in *chachma*: **he's a real *chacham*, but he knows what a *chacham* he is**. He feels that it is *mamash* his own *chachma*. And so all his *middos* and virtues he knows and feels, standing out greatly.

phrases.he: ובהסתעפות יוצא מזה בחינת רע,
phrases.en: When it goes down into *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, it comes out of that a real *ra*

phrases.he: כמו המרגיש עצמו לחסדן יצא מזה הסתעפות חסד רק להתייהר ורק לגרמיה, כמו חסד ישמעאל וכהאי גוונא והוא דמיון להשתלשלות דנוגה דבריאה שנסתעף מנוגה דאצילות שמיעוטה רע על כל פנים בבחינת לגרמיה ויוהרא דהתנשאות יש הנפרד כו' (וכמו שמהתלהבות הבולט בהרגשת עצמו בתפלה, יכעס על המנגדו להכותו ולרודפו כשנוגע בכבודו)

blocks.text: **When it goes down into *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, it comes out of that a real *ra***. One who feels himself a man of *chesed*: out of it comes a *chesed* only for self-importance and *l'garmei* (for himself), like the *chesed* of Yishmael.

Like the Arabs. He will do the *chesed*, but because he wants the honor, to be a big shot; and if you do not acknowledge what a great host he is, he will get mad, and he might kill you. That is the next thing the text says.

sensitivity.reason: Applies "the chesed of Yishmael" to the Arabs: hospitality for honor, and they might kill you if it is not acknowledged.

blocks.text: So *noga* of *Beriya*, which spreads from *noga* of *Atzilus*, is at least a little evil: *l'garmei*, the haughtiness of a separate *yesh*. Like one whose fervor in prayer stands out in his feeling of himself, and who gets angry at whoever holds him back when it touches his honor. Like the people who get mad and start shouting when the kids make noise in shul: it disturbs their *tefilla* (prayer). And really, that can be even in *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: וכך אמרו שטן ופנינה לשם שמים נתכוונו, שזהו בחינת נוגה דאצילות, ונתן עיניו במקדש ראשון והחריבו זהו מבחינת קנאה של נחש הקדמוני,
בחינת יש ולגרמיה בבחינת רע קצת,
phrases.en: *yesh*, and for his own self, and a little bit of evil

phrases.he: אף על פי שקנאה זאת באה מצד הכרתו וקירובו, כי כלום מתקנא כו'

blocks.text: So they said: the Satan and Penina meant it for the sake of Heaven, and that is *noga* of *Atzilus*. The Satan goes all the way up to *noga* of *Atzilus*: even in *Atzilus* there is a Satan. And he set his eyes on the First Temple and destroyed it. Penina made Chana angry for the sake of Heaven, so that she would pray to have children; but still, she should not have done it.

The difference: the man who gets angry at whoever holds him back does it when it *mamash* touches his honor; the Satan of *Atzilus* gets mad at the children not for his honor but for the sake of Heaven. Rabbi Markel knows people like that. It is a holy thing, and they think it is a holy thing: they will show you the halacha in the book that you are supposed to throw all the kids out of the shul.

This is from the jealousy of the primordial serpent: a *yesh*, for his own self, and a little bit of evil, though this jealousy comes from his recognition and closeness. He understands how holy the shul is. How could someone be jealous that they are making noise in the shul, if he does not know the holiness of the shul?

phrases.he: ונוגה דיצירה חציו רע לקטרג ממש, כמו ויבא גם השטן כו' ויאמר החנם ירא איוב כו' עד בחינת נוגה דעשיה רובו רע לפעול כל דין קשה
וזהו חיותו ממש
phrases.en: He actually loves to do *din*

phrases.he: ונקרא רצועא בישא לאלקאה כו', כמו העלוקה שמושכת פסולת הדם כו' כך נאמר לעלוקה
כו' הב הב כו',
phrases.en: Give me, give me

phrases.he: שזהו שרש הגיהנום שעל ראש רשעים יחול כו' כידוע

blocks.text: *Noga* of *Yetzira* is half evil, to accuse *mamash*, like "the Satan came too" in *Iyov*: "Does Iyov fear G-d for nothing?" After all, You gave him so much money. Down to *noga* of *Asiya*, mostly evil, to carry out every harsh judgement, and that is its very life: **He actually loves to do *din***.

It is called the evil strap for whipping, like the leech that sucks the waste of the blood; and again, if you know how to use a leech, it is medicinal. Of it is said, to the leech: **Give me, give me**. And this is the root of *Gehinom*, which rests on the head of the wicked.

sections.title: The three impure kelipos, and the end of the book
sections.summary: Below *noga* come the three impure *kelipos*, the *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* of *kelipa*: utter evil, with no refinement until the future, "meaning tomorrow". Then the *hadran* on the whole book.

phrases.he: וג' קליפות הטמאות הן כמו נחש שרף ועקרב שבמדבר העמים בחינת כתר דקליפה שהן
רע גמור
phrases.en: Totally bad

phrases.he: בלי תערובת הטוב כלל וכלל וזהו הנקרא רשע ורע לו,
שאין להם בירור עדיין כלל,
phrases.en: there's no *birur* for them at all

phrases.he: רק לעתיד דכתיב ואת רוח הטומאה אעביר לגמרי כו' וכידוע ודי למבין

blocks.question: What does "this is the root of Gehinom" refer to?
blocks.text: To all of these. And the lower it is, the stronger: it is backwards. The strongest is not in *Atzilus* but *davka* down here, all the way to the leech, the lowest part of *kelipas noga*. And from there come the three impure *kelipos*.

These last three lines are the next *hishtalshelus*. *Kelipas noga* is basically the *Atzilus* of *kelipa*, and it has its own *ABYA*, which the text has just described. From there come the three impure *kelipos*, the *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* of *kelipa*: the snake, the serpent and the scorpion of the wilderness of the nations.

They are *Keser* of *kelipa*: utter evil with no mixture of good at all. What does *Keser* of *kelipa* mean, when the nations are *mamash* *Asiya*? Upside down. **Totally bad**: their whole delight is only in this world, and only in bad things. That is what they love.

sensitivity.reason: Of the impure kelipos of "the wilderness of the nations": the nations' whole delight is only in this world and only in bad things.
sensitivity.publishable: They are *Keser* of *kelipa*: utter evil with no mixture of good at all. What does *Keser* of *kelipa* mean, when the nations are *mamash* *Asiya*? Upside down. **Totally bad**.

blocks.text: This is called "a wicked man who has evil": that is *mamash* what they love, to go to war. And **there's no *birur* for them at all**, only in the future, as it is written, "I will remove the spirit of impurity" entirely. And that will happen in the future: meaning tomorrow.

sensitivity.reason: Says of them (the nations of the line before) that what they love is to go to war.
sensitivity.publishable: This is called "a wicked man who has evil". And **there's no *birur* for them at all**, only in the future, as it is written, "I will remove the spirit of impurity" entirely. And that will happen in the future: meaning tomorrow.

phrases.he: סליק שער היחוד

blocks.text: *Hadran alach Shaar HaYichud* (we will return to you, Gate of Unity), said three times. There was a *minyan*, so the special *Kaddish* can be said. And with that the whole *hishtalshelus* is done.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the kelipa come before the fruit, and what does the placenta show about its purpose?
Why does whatever spreads from the essence have a menaged, and how far does its opposition go?
If the analysis is correct, where is the breaking, and how can a right premise lead to a wrong act?
Why is the chachma of kelipa called cunning rather than wisdom?
How is the partzuf of kelipa a mirror of holiness, and where is the worst of it?
What is noga of Atzilus, and what does it become as it comes down to Asiya?
